title: AEGP session stream ID and native indexed-group admissibility probe
question: How do native Shape Contents and ordinary Effect Parade differ in their stream-identity metadata, grouping flags and AEGP_CanAddStream matrix?

hypotheses.prediction: Shape Contents and Effect Parade have indexed-group surface with distinct supported child type names
hypotheses.falsified_by: AE2026 host produces indistinguishable per-group CanAdd accept/reject matrices for observed types

hypotheses.prediction: AEGP_GetUniqueStreamID associates a session-specific numeric identifier to valid stream refs
hypotheses.falsified_by: Real-host API consistently reports error/zero for tested native shape streams

factors: Shape Layer with nested path/fill and transform
Captured before/after reorder or Undo in same AE session
procedure: Quit AE normally before deploying compiled probe; replace old AEX and restart.
Use Animation > ShapeLayerAE: Dump Stream Tree on native Shape Layer and copy all 3 TSVs to uniquely named captures.
Repeat for ordinary layer plus effect and separately for native group reorder/Undo.
Record precise AE version, hashes, screenshots/error dialogs; compare E2-X output.
Never infer third-party custom factory registration merely from CanAdd results.
conclusion: C++ probe compiled (not yet loaded or tested in AE). Source snapshot and build receipt are reproducible; all host behavior is pending.
limitations: Session-unique ID is not stable project identity
CanAdd on existing Indexed Group is not create-native-type API
User workspace should not be modified or reloaded without consent
